chapter: Precision, the union and learning to read
title: Morale, loyalty and hours on the road
summary: Crawford says members gave their hearts to the band and played four to five hours a night.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, with all of the travelling and playing these one-nighters and having to sleep on the bus and all of this, how did you all keep up the energy to --
Yeah, how did you keep that up to play?

Well, I'll tell you what, Stanley. Everybody that played in that band had their hearts and souls in it. All those that didn't, they knew they were in the wrong place. They had to go somewhere else. You just don't come in Lunceford's band and figure that you're going to run yourself and do what you want to do, no, not in Lunceford's band. Yet, we were happy all the time. We did what Lunceford wanted us to do, because he was a leader of men. Pardon me.

Yeah, you know what I'm saying, in terms of -- like, because, like, if you're playing those one-nighters, there's a lot of, like, time when you don't sleep too well or something and you got to play. How many hours did you all used to have to play a night, if you were playing? How many sets did you play?
Yeah, from 8:30 or 9:00 until 2:00 in the morning. Four or five hours. That was -- all bands had to play, mostly.
